title: Sheol: The Place of the Dead
lead: Sheol is the Hebrew Bible's name for the realm of the dead, pictured deep beneath the earth, a place of silence and shadow where all the dead go. The KJV often translates it "hell" or "the grave." Later texts hope for rescue from Sheol, and the New Testament uses the Greek equivalent, Hades.

sections.b: Sheol is first named by Jacob, mourning Joseph (Genesis 37:35). It is "down" (Numbers 16:30–33), a place where no one praises God (Psalm 6:5; Isaiah 38:18) and where there is no work or knowledge (Ecclesiastes 9:10). Yet God is present even there (Psalm 139:8), and the psalmists hope to be ransomed from it (Psalm 16:10; 49:15). Isaiah 14:9–15 pictures the dead kings in Sheol greeting the fallen king of Babylon. The Septuagint translates Sheol as Hades, the word used when Peter applies Psalm 16 to Jesus' resurrection (Acts 2:27–31) and when Revelation says Death and Hades are thrown into the lake of fire (Revelation 20:13–14).

sections.b:
Between the Testaments, some Jewish writers divided the world of the dead. In 1 Enoch 22 the spirits of the dead wait in separate hollows, the righteous apart from sinners, until the judgment. The New Testament uses this picture: in Jesus' parable the rich man is in torment in Hades while Lazarus is at Abraham's side (Luke 16:23); Jesus says "the gates of Hades" will not overpower his church (Matthew 16:18); and the risen Christ holds "the keys of death and of Hades" (Revelation 1:18).

Readers disagree about what Sheol is. Many scholars, Jewish and Christian, hold that in most of the Hebrew Bible it is a neutral, shadowy grave for all, and that ideas of reward and punishment after death came later (Daniel 12:2). Rabbinic Judaism spoke of Gan Eden and Gehinnom as places of reward and purification. Among Christians, some see Sheol as the temporary waiting place of all the dead before the resurrection; others hold that it was divided from the start, and some traditions teach that Christ freed the righteous dead from it (compare 1 Peter 3:19; Ephesians 4:8–9).
